description:
The stock market is still near record highs, AI spending is still exploding, and millions of retirement accounts are still pouring money into the biggest tech companies on Earth.
But some of the world’s most successful investors are quietly moving the other way.

This video explores the warning signs that often appear before major market crashes. Billionaire investors reducing exposure, insiders selling shares, record index concentration, massive corporate spending, rising debt, and valuations increasingly dependent on future profits that haven’t arrived yet.
The Magnificent Seven now dominate the S&P 500, meaning even supposedly diversified retirement funds are heavily exposed to the same handful of AI-driven companies. Meanwhile, hedge funds and billionaire investors have been cutting tech positions, building cash reserves, and rotating into gold, commodities, infrastructure, and other defensive assets.

title: This is What “Always” Happens Before a Market Crash

author: The Infographics Show
description:
Meta spent decades protected by Section 230, the law that shields platforms from liability for what their users post. Then prosecutors found a way around it - Don’t attack the content, attack the product itself.

This video explores the massive legal case that threatened Meta with penalties reportedly reaching as high as $1.4 trillion. Attorneys argued that features like the Like button, infinite scroll, notifications, and engagement algorithms were deliberately engineered to keep users, especially children, coming back for more. Leaked internal research made the case even more dangerous. Meta’s own documents showed the company knew Instagram could worsen body-image issues, anxiety, depression, and eating disorders among teenagers, while whistleblowers alleged executives failed to act aggressively enough.
